subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After the persistence-ordering race is repaired, should OpenClaw accept the new permanent compaction timeout key and generic synchronous command-queue timeout callback?
rationale: The blocking race has a bounded mechanical repair, but the config and shared queue callback become durable operator and internal API contracts that cannot be selected safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Accept both contracts
options.body: Keep the opt-in config and generic callback after persistence ownership is fixed and focused compatibility tests cover disabled, zero, and positive values.

options.title: Reuse existing lifecycle primitives
options.body: Rework the repair around existing abort or release signals so the new config key or generic callback is unnecessary.

options.title: Pause for broader redesign
options.body: Defer the PR if correct ownership requires a cancellable maintenance or transcript transaction contract beyond this bounded repair.

recommendation.title: Accept both contracts
recommendation.body: Keep the opt-in config and generic callback after persistence ownership is fixed and focused compatibility tests cover disabled, zero, and positive values.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main maintenance checkpoint and transcript persistence lifecycle trace to his recent refactor commit.
